meta.promptText: Which vitamin C serum should I buy for dark spots and dull skin in India?

response.text:
For **dark spots and dull skin in India**, the safest “best buy” for most people is a **stable 10% vitamin C serum** with added brightening/support ingredients like **niacinamide, vitamin E, ferulic acid, or hyaluronic acid**.[2][15][8]

If you want a simple pick-by-use-case:

| Need | Best fit from the results | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Beginner / sensitive skin** | **Pilgrim 10% Vitamin C Face Serum** | 10% vitamin C with niacinamide and soothing support ingredients; described as a gentle daily option.[2] |
| **Stubborn dark spots** | **La Roche-Posay Pure 12% Vitamin C** | Highlighted as best overall for pigmentation/dark spots, with L-ascorbic acid plus hyaluronic acid and salicylic acid.[1] |
| **Budget, stronger potency** | **The Ordinary Vitamin C 23%** | Listed as a high-potency budget option for stubborn pigmentation.[1] |
| **Stable formula for Indian climate** | **Ethyl ascorbic acid serums** | One source says ethyl ascorbic acid is more stable in India’s humidity/heat than pure ascorbic acid.[3] |

A practical recommendation: if your skin is *new to vitamin C* or easily irritated, start with **10%** rather than jumping to 20%+.[2][15][8] For *faster dark-spot fading*, stronger formulas can work, but they may also irritate more, especially if your skin barrier is sensitive.[15][8]

If you want the **single best general recommendation**, choose a **10–15% stable vitamin C serum with niacinamide or vitamin E/ferulic acid** and use it **every morning under sunscreen**.[2][15][9] That combination is the most consistently supported across the results for brightness, dullness, and post-acne marks.[2][9][13]

If you tell me your **budget, skin type, and whether you want fragrance-free**, I can narrow this to **1–3 exact products** to buy in India.
